newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Aktif factoring sees 70 trln lira 97 turnover.
newsitem.headline: Turk Aktif factoring sees 70 trln lira 97 turnover.

text.p: Aktif Finans Factoring Hizmetleri A.S., a leading Turkish factoring company, targets 70 trillion lira of turnover this year, after an estimated 30 trillion lira in 1996, a senior company official said.

"The factoring sector grew last year despite difficulties. Our turnover doubled to 30 trillion lira from 14 trillion in 1995. Our 1997 target is 70 trillion lira," Ferruh Tanay, general manager of the company, told Reuters in an interview.
He said the company planned to raise its capital to one trillion lira from 250 billion this year and increase its current market share which stands at around 20 percent.
Aktif Finans shares listed on the Istanbul Stock Exchange traded at 3,850 lira on Tuesday, up from Monday's 3,800 close.
Factoring services provided to exporters made up about half of the company's 1996 turnover which was directed mainly at food, textile and durables firms.

"Growing turnover helped to raise our profitability in 1996. Our profits rose above the inflation rate (in 1996) and our total assets expanded to about 8.5 trillion lira from 2.5-3 trillion a year ago and became more liquid," Tanay said.
Turkey's 1996 year-on-year consumer inflation was 79.8 percent and wholesale inflation was 84.9 percent.

The company diversified its products and set up a separate leasing company last year due to customer demand, Tanay said, adding that the purchase of Aktif Finans' 55 percent stake by construction and financial Dogus group would have positive effects on operations.
"Dogus group can support our growth and developments plans," Tanay said.
He said new entries into the Turkish factoring sector had an overcrowding effect in 1996 when the overall market turnover reached $1.5 billion, up from $900 million a year ago.

"The number of companies in the (factoring) sector rose to 60 last year. This figure is too high, even for some developed countries," Tanay said, adding that only about six or seven firms engaged in international activities.
Competition which became more stiff forced companies to cut prices which in turn narrowed their profit margins.
Last year's political and economic uncertainities were also negative factors for factoring because any slowdown or acceleration in trade activites immediately reflected on the sector's turnover.
"Despite these negative factors, the sector grew in dollar terms. Companies in Turkey think of factoring firms when they are in need of cash. But the sector needs to improve itself," Tanay said.
Aktif Finans reported 222 billion lira of net profits in the first nine months of 1996, up from 140.8 billion in the same 1995 period.
